data.narrative:
Climeworks, a Series F climate and energy technology company founded by Christoph Gebald and Jan Wurzbacher, has raised over $1.0 billion to date. The valuation exercise draws on a comparison universe of 9 same-sector peers: 1 public company and 8 private firms including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBolt Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

A stage-progression methodology was the primary applicable triangulation approach. Using the $1.0 billion total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a typical Series F step-up multiplier of 1.3x yields an implied valuation of $1.3 billion. A peer-median approach was not viable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow climate and energy peer set; only one same-stage peer was identified, falling short of the three-datapoint threshold required for statistical relevance. Relying on an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable bias.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $1.1 billion to $1.5 billion, with a median point of $1.3 billion. This range reflects moderate confidence given reliance on a single method. Key uncertainties include the limited comparable set at Series F stage, the relative nascency of the climate tech sector, and the absence of recent disclosed valuations for direct peers. Capital deployment velocity and commercial traction on deployed assets would be critical to validating upside assumptions within this range.
